question: Where can I get a list of drinking water treatment plants in the United States, with location, capacity and operator?

answer.summary: No national list of drinking-water treatment plants with location, capacity and operator was found. EPA's SDWIS (Envirofacts API) and ECHO list systems and regulatory facilities: 246,214 treatment-type rows, which are entry or monitoring points without coordinates or capacity. Iowa DNR publishes a point layer of treatment sub-facilities (5,142 rows, duplicated, many at ZIP centroids) without capacity. Capacity appears only in operator documents, such as Metropolitan Water District's five plants. Supply zones and population served were not used as substitutes.
main_caveats: SDWIS 'TP' rows (246,214; 163,265 active) are regulatory entry or monitoring points such as filter effluent or booster stations, not physical plants, and have no coordinates or capacity.
Population served and service area describe a system, not a plant: the wholesaler MWD system shows population served 0 in SDWIS.
California's dataset named 'Public Water System Facilities' has one row per system (7,603) and its 'Treatment Plant Class' is an operator grade.
Iowa's layer duplicates rows (5,142 rows for about 2,603 sub-facilities) and 1,976 positions are ZIP centroids with 3,300 m accuracy.
Capacity is nominal and found only in operator documents tested for one operator.
Contact fields in SDWIS hold personal data; none were reproduced.
answer.confidence_reason: Counts and fields tested in SDWIS, ECHO, California, Iowa and one operator; no national plant list or capacity source found, and several state sources failed to load.

attributes.note: Iowa DNR gives plant points (5,142 rows, 38% ZIP-centroid, 3,300 m); MWD gives only the city; SDWIS and ECHO give no coordinates.
attributes.gap_note: Only Iowa has plant points among states tested. The Florida (SFWMD) potable treatment plant layer reported by search timed out after 60 s, and a data.gov record and a NASA HIFLD mirror were not reachable. Other states were not tested.

attributes.note: Capacity in mgd was found only in operator documents: five Metropolitan Water District plants (220 to 750 mgd). No capacity field in SDWIS, ECHO, California or Iowa.
attributes.gap_note: Nothing nationwide; state layers reported to hold capacity (South Florida Water Management District) could not be opened. Other operators and states were not tested.

attributes.note: SDWIS and ECHO give the system, owner type and name; MWD's own documents name the operator of five plants. The Iowa layer names the system only.
attributes.gap_note: System names and owner types are not per-plant operators: SDWIS has no operator field at facility level and contact fields hold personal data. Operators beyond MWD were not checked.

coverage.geographic: United States and territories (state and tribal primacy agencies)

unit.value: WATER_SYSTEM: one row per public water system. WATER_SYSTEM_FACILITY: one row per regulatory facility record (well, intake, treatment entry point, sampling point, connection, distribution system), not per physical plant.

inclusion_rule.value: Facility rows include inactive records: 246,214 rows of type TP, 163,265 of them active.

update_frequency.value: Not stated on the pages read.

key_fields.meaning: System identifier, name and type (CWS community, NTNCWS, TNCWS).
Facility record: TP treatment, IN intake, WL well, TM treatment-monitoring point, CC consecutive connection, DS distribution system; A active, I inactive.
System-level owner type, population served and wholesaler flag; not plant attributes.
System contact fields; org_name held a person's name in the system inspected. Personal data: not reproduced.

how_to_use.example_result: HTTP 200 JSON listing the treatment-type rows of PWSID CA1910087 (Metropolitan Water District of Southern California, La Verne): effluent points of the Weymouth, Jensen, Diemer, Mills and Skinner plants, with no coordinates or capacity.
steps: Count with /WATER_SYSTEM_FACILITY/FACILITY_TYPE_CODE/TP/FACILITY_ACTIVITY_CODE/A/COUNT/JSON; add PRIMACY_AGENCY_CODE/<state> to limit to a state.
Read facility_name to see what the TP row represents (effluent, entry point, filter influent, booster station).
Join pwsid to WATER_SYSTEM for system name, type, owner type and population served.
Use another source for coordinates and capacity.
reading_traps: A TP row is a regulatory monitoring or entry-point record: names seen include 'FILTER EFFLUENT', 'TANK EFFLUENT, ENTRY POINT', 'BOOSTER STATION' and 'WELL 01 - TREATED'; one plant can have several TP rows.
The facility table carries no coordinates and no capacity.
population_served_count is 0 for the wholesaler CA1910087; population is a system attribute and not a plant capacity.

problems: records_total is the count of facility rows with facility_type_code TP (all activity states).
No SDWIS documentation page was opened; field meanings come from observed values and codes, so code meanings (for example TM) were not confirmed.
